## 1. One Term journey, as it appears in the audit log

Every line below is what an operator or auditor would actually see. Note what is
absent: no name, no PAN, no mobile, no email, no date of birth, and no raw
upstream payload. Outbound calls carry a SHA-256 hash of the **masked** body, so
two identical submissions are provably identical without either being readable.

2026-08-13T09:15:00Z  audit eventId=evt-dec3 action=QUOTE_JOB_CREATED outcome=SUCCESS resourceType=QUOTE_JOB resourceId=job-quote-9a1 actorId=rm-4471 journeyId=journey-7f3a traceId=3d9a1c4e8b2f4a17 metadata={sumAssured=5000000, lob=TERM}

## 2. What a proposal body looks like before and after masking

This is the payload that would otherwise reach a log or an audit hash.

**Before** (never written anywhere in this form):

```json
{
  "applicationNo": "APP-2026-0417",
  "proposer": {
    "firstName": "Asha",
    "lastName": "Rao",
    "dob": "1990-01-15",
    "pan": "ABCDE1234F",
    "mobile": "9876543210",
    "email": "asha.rao@example.com"
  },
  "nominee": { "name": "Ravi Rao", "dob": "2015-06-02" },
  "sumAssured": 5000000
}
```

**After `PiiMasker.maskJson`** — this is what the service is willing to expose:

```json
{
  "applicationNo" : "APP-2026-0417",
  "proposer" : {
    "firstName" : "A***",
    "lastName" : "R***",
    "dob" : "****-**-**",
    "pan" : "*****1234F",
    "mobile" : "******3210",
    "email" : "a***@e***.com"
  },
  "nominee" : {
    "name" : "R***",
    "dob" : "****-**-**"
  },
  "sumAssured" : 5000000
}
```

Field-level behaviour, exercised by `PiiMaskerTest`:

| Input | Masked | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| `Asha` | `A***` | First initial only |
| `9876543210` | `******3210` | Last 4 digits retained for support lookups |
| `asha.rao@example.com` | `a***@e***.com` | Local part and domain both reduced |
| `ABCDE1234F` | `*****1234F` | Last 5 retained; leading letters replaced with `*` so the result cannot match a PAN pattern |
| `1990-01-15` | `****-**-**` | Date of birth removed entirely |

## 3. Free-text masking

PII does not only arrive in known field names. An error message or a nested
string is pattern-scanned as well:

```text
in : Rejected for proposer ABCDE1234F (contact 9876543210, asha.rao@example.com)
out: Rejected for proposer *****1234F (contact ******3210, a***@e***.com)
```
